examples.title: HR table: average salary by department
examples.description: 30 employee records. Aggregation over a filtered table.
examples.question: Among active employees, which 3 departments have the highest average salary? Give the department, the number of active employees and the average salary rounded to a whole number.

examples.title: E-commerce: revenue per country (nested orders)
examples.description: 15 orders with a nested customer and item list. Filter, group, sum.
examples.question: For orders with status paid, shipped or delivered, what is the number of orders and the total revenue (sum of total) per customer country? Sort by revenue, highest first.

examples.title: Ops: which service is failing? (logs)
examples.description: 60 log events. Counting by level and averaging a numeric field.
examples.question: For each service, count the ERROR and WARN events and give the average latency_ms of its ERROR events (rounded; null if none). Sort by ERROR count, highest first.

examples.title: Agent tool result: pick the best search hits
examples.description: A web_search tool result with 15 hits, as an agent would receive it.
examples.question: Which 3 results best answer 'how should agents manage memory'? Give the rank, the url and a one-sentence reason for each.

examples.title: Analytics: best days in a time series
examples.description: 28 days of metrics. Sorting a time series.
examples.question: Which 3 days had the highest revenue? Give the date, revenue, visits and signups.

examples.title: Developer data: filter repositories
examples.description: 30 repositories with topic lists. Multi-condition filter and sort.
examples.question: List the repositories that are not archived, are written in Python or Rust and have more than 10,000 stars, sorted by stars (highest first). Include the license.

examples.title: Support: unassigned urgent tickets
examples.description: 25 support tickets with nulls. Triage filter.
examples.question: Which open tickets with priority high or urgent have no assignee? Sort them by created date, oldest first.

examples.title: Inventory: what to reorder and how much
examples.description: 25 products. Comparison between two fields plus arithmetic.
examples.question: Which products have stock below their reorder_level? For each, suggest an order quantity that covers 30 days of sales: 30 × daily_sales − stock, rounded up.

examples.title: Scheduling: find a common free hour
examples.description: Calendar events of three people. Reasoning over time intervals.
examples.question: Working hours are 09:00–17:00. List every 1-hour slot starting on the full hour on Tue when Ada, Alan and Grace are all free (no event overlaps the slot).

examples.title: Extraction: emails to structured orders (output format)
examples.description: Free text in, structured data out. Shows the answer format saving output tokens.
examples.question: Extract every order from these emails: the customer name, the product (as named in our catalogue: Keyboard, Monitor 27", USB-C cable, Headset), the quantity and the delivery date as YYYY-MM-DD.

examples.title: Invoices: overdue and unpaid
examples.description: Amounts in grosze and status codes 0/1/2 — explained only in the metadata.
examples.question: Which invoices are unpaid and overdue on 2026-10-20? Give the number and the gross amount in PLN.

examples.title: Departures: delayed flights
examples.description: Delay is in minutes and times are UTC.
examples.question: Which flights are delayed by more than 30 minutes? Longest delay first.

examples.title: School grades: average per class
examples.description: Polish 1–6 grade scale (6 is the best) — said in the metadata.
examples.question: What is the average math grade in each class, rounded to 2 decimals?

examples.title: Crypto prices: top movers
examples.description: 24h change is in basis points (1/100 of a percent) — only the metadata says so.
examples.question: Which 3 coins rose the most in 24 hours? Give the change in percent.

examples.title: Weather: Fahrenheit forecast
examples.description: Temperatures are in °F; the question asks about °C.
examples.question: On which days will the high stay below 10 °C? Give the high in °C, rounded to 1 decimal.

examples.title: Bank account: spending per category
examples.description: Negative amounts are spending, in cents.
examples.question: How much was spent in each category (money going out), in PLN? Most first.

examples.title: Servers: CPU above 80 %
examples.description: Load is in per mille (‰), not percent.
examples.question: Which hosts use more than 80 % CPU? Give the CPU in percent, highest first.

examples.title: Web vitals: slow pages
examples.description: Largest Contentful Paint in milliseconds, budget 2.5 s.
examples.question: Which pages have an LCP worse than 2500 ms? Slowest first.

examples.title: CRM: leads in the proposal stage
examples.description: Stage is a code 1–4.
examples.question: Which leads are in the proposal stage? Highest score first.

examples.title: Shipments: weight per carrier
examples.description: Weight is in grams.
examples.question: What is the total weight in kilograms per carrier? Heaviest first.

examples.title: Recipes: nut-free and quick
examples.description: Lists inside records.
examples.question: Which recipes contain no nuts of any kind and take at most 45 minutes?

examples.title: Films: best-rated drama
examples.description: Genre lists inside records.
examples.question: Which film tagged drama has the highest rating? Give the title, year and rating.

examples.title: Git log: most active authors
examples.description: Twenty commits.
examples.question: Which 3 authors made the most commits? Ties alphabetically.

examples.title: Hotel: revenue per room type
examples.description: Nights × nightly rate.
examples.question: What is the revenue (nights × rate) per room type? Highest first.

examples.title: HR: approved leave per person
examples.description: Status is a one-letter code.
examples.question: How many days of approved leave does each person have? Most first.

examples.title: IoT tags: low battery
examples.description: Battery is in millivolts.
examples.question: Which devices have a battery below 3.3 V? Give the voltage in volts, lowest first.

examples.title: API: slow endpoints
examples.description: p95 latency in microseconds.
examples.question: Which endpoints have a p95 latency above 200 ms? Give it in ms (1 decimal), slowest first.

examples.title: Menu: vegan dishes under 25 PLN
examples.description: Prices are in grosze.
examples.question: Which vegan dishes cost less than 25 PLN? Give the price in PLN.

examples.title: Library: overdue loans
examples.description: Dates as text.
examples.question: Which loans are overdue on 2026-10-15? Oldest due date first.

examples.title: Company cars: service due
examples.description: Odometer and last service.
examples.question: Which cars have driven more than 15,000 km since the last service? Most first; give the distance.

examples.title: Shopping cart: total after discounts
examples.description: Prices in grosze, discounts in basis points.
examples.question: What is the cart total in PLN after the per-item discounts?

examples.title: Survey: share of agreement
examples.description: Likert answers 1–5 as numbers.
examples.question: For each statement, what percent of answers agree (agree or strongly agree)? Round to whole percent.

examples.title: Football: most goals scored
examples.description: Score as [home, away].
examples.question: Which team scored the most goals in these matches, and how many?

examples.title: Energy meter: kWh per day
examples.description: Readings in watt-hours.
examples.question: What is the total energy per day in kWh (2 decimals)?

examples.title: Job board: remote and well paid
examples.description: Salary ranges per month.
examples.question: Which remote jobs pay at least 20,000 at the top of the range? Highest first.

examples.title: GitHub: open bugs
examples.description: Label lists per issue.
examples.question: Which issues are open and labelled bug?

examples.title: Support: SLA breaches
examples.description: SLA limits per priority are in the metadata.
examples.question: Which tickets have breached their SLA, and by how many hours?

examples.title: Exchange rates: convert 500 EUR
examples.description: One base currency, a list of rates.
examples.question: How much is 500 EUR in each currency (2 decimals)?

examples.title: Reviews: rating of verified buyers
examples.description: Verified purchases are tagged — only in the metadata.
examples.question: What is the average star rating of verified purchases only (2 decimals)?

examples.title: Office: rooms for 8 with a projector
examples.description: Equipment lists.
examples.question: Which rooms seat at least 8 people and have a projector?

examples.title: Portfolio: profit per position
examples.description: Average buy price vs last price.
examples.question: What is the profit or loss of each PLN position (qty × (last − avg), 2 decimals)?

examples.title: Parking: free spots per level
examples.description: Occupancy as 0/1.
examples.question: How many spots are free on each level?

examples.title: Newsletter: campaigns above 25 % opens
examples.description: Open and click rates in per mille.
examples.question: Which campaigns have an open rate above 25 %? Give the rate in percent, highest first.

examples.title: DNS zone: short TTLs
examples.description: TTL in seconds; documentation IP ranges.
examples.question: Which records have a TTL below 300 seconds?

examples.title: Timesheets: hours per project
examples.description: Time logged in minutes.
examples.question: How many hours were logged per project (2 decimals)? Most first.

examples.title: CI: failed runs per branch
examples.description: Status is an exit-code-like number.
examples.question: How many runs failed on each branch? Most first.

examples.title: Nutrition: protein per portion
examples.description: Values per 100 g, portions in grams.
examples.question: Which 3 foods give the most protein per portion? Give grams of protein (1 decimal).

examples.title: Shop orders: status codes, cents and test orders
examples.description: Order status is a code, amounts are in cents, two orders are tests — only the metadata says so.
examples.question: Which real orders (not tests) were refunded, and how much was each in euros?

examples.title: Sensors: tenths of a degree, UTC times, calibrating
examples.description: Temperatures are tenths of °C, times are UTC, two sensors are being calibrated and their values are not valid.
examples.question: Which room was the warmest, using only valid readings? Give the sensor, the room and the temperature in °C.

examples.title: Staff: levels as codes, monthly salaries, contractors
examples.description: Level is a code, salary is monthly in PLN, two people are contractors — written only in the metadata.
examples.question: List the senior people who are employees (not contractors) with their yearly salary in PLN.

examples.title: Inventory: reorder levels and discontinued items
examples.description: min is the reorder level and two items are discontinued (never reordered) — only the metadata explains it.
examples.question: Which items must be reordered and how many pieces are missing to reach the reorder level?

examples.title: Flat table: users
examples.description: A list of records sharing one header: field names are written once, every record is a (…) tuple in header order.
examples.question: Which active users are admins?

examples.title: Nested records: orders with customer and items
examples.description: Headers nest: customer is a record <…> inside the record, items a list of records <[…]>; nested values stay positional.
examples.question: What is the total (qty × price) of every paid order?

examples.title: Agent tool result: web search hits
examples.description: A record with simple fields and a list of records — the typical tool output an agent puts back into the context.
examples.question: Which results have a score of at least 0.9?

examples.title: Time series: a week of metrics
examples.description: Numbers stay numbers (no quotes); a time series is just a list of records with a date field.
examples.question: Which day had the most signups, and what was the revenue that day?

examples.title: Logs: which service is failing?
examples.description: Repeated rows are where AK-DATA saves most: the five field names appear once instead of eight times.
examples.question: How many errors does each service have? Most errors first.

examples.title: Irregular data: a record that does not fit the header
examples.description: The third agent has temperature instead of max_steps, so it is written as <any> {key:value} with its own keys — still lossless.
examples.question: Which agent can use the most tools, and how many?

examples.title: Type overrides: values that differ from the header
examples.description: When one value has another type than its column, it is prefixed with <type> — <number> 3001, <string> "on order"; null fits every type.
examples.question: Which products cannot be sold right now (no price, no stock, or stock not a number)?

examples.title: Lists inside records: repositories with topics
examples.description: A field can hold a list of values: topics:[string] in the header, ["llm","rust"] or [] in the record.
examples.question: Which repositories that are not archived have the topic rust? Most stars first.

examples.title: Lists of lists: a distance matrix
examples.description: Nested lists need no header beyond [[number]]: rows are plain [ … ] lists.
examples.question: Which two cities are farthest apart, and how far?

examples.title: Missing values: support tickets
examples.description: A nested record that is missing is <null> null (or null): the header still describes the record when it is there.
examples.question: Which urgent tickets have nobody assigned?

examples.title: Names with spaces and symbols
examples.description: Field names that are not simple identifiers go in backticks: `user id`, `e-mail`, `2fa`.
examples.question: Which users do not have 2FA enabled?

examples.title: Named types: @User defined once, used three times
examples.description: @User<…> names a header; lead:@User and members:[@User] reuse it. Hand-written AK-DATA (the encoder writes inline headers).
examples.question: How many people are in the team, including the lead? Give the team name too.

examples.title: Comments, attributes and tags
examples.description: /* comments */, $attr=value, #tags and // … // blocks are notes for the reader: they are skipped when decoding, the data is unchanged.
examples.question: What is the total monthly revenue (mrr) per plan? Highest first.

examples.title: Schema and instance metadata
examples.description: Metadata on the header ($required, $unit, $maxItems, comments) describes every record; metadata on a value ($verified, #featured, #discontinued) describes one record. Both are skipped when decoding — the JSON is the same — but a model reads them.
examples.question: Which products are verified and not discontinued? Give the sku and the price in EUR.

examples.title: Calendar: lists of [start, end] pairs
examples.description: Records can hold lists of lists; the header says busy:[[string]] once for every person.
examples.question: Which full hours (start on the hour, 60 minutes) are free for everyone?
